title: Architects, Except Landscape and Naval
description: Plan and design structures, such as private residences, office buildings, theaters, factories, and other structural property.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Integrate engineering elements into unified architectural designs.
Plan layouts of structural architectural projects.
Plan or design structures such as residences, office buildings, theatres, factories, or other structural properties in accordance with environmental, safety, or other regulations.
Design structures that incorporate environmentally friendly building practices or concepts, such as Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) standards.
Design or plan construction of green building projects to minimize adverse environmental impact or conserve energy.
Prepare information regarding design, structure specifications, materials, color, equipment, estimated costs, or construction time.
Prepare contract documents for building contractors.
Administer construction contracts.
Represent clients in obtaining bids or awarding construction contracts.
Prepare operating and maintenance manuals, studies, or reports.
Develop final construction plans that include aesthetic representations of the structure or details for its construction.
Prepare scale drawings or architectural designs, using computer-aided design or other tools.
Create three-dimensional or interactive representations of designs, using computer-assisted design software.
Design environmentally sound structural upgrades to existing buildings, such as natural lighting systems, green roofs, or rainwater collection systems.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Consult with clients to determine functional or spatial requirements of structures.
Meet with clients to review or discuss architectural drawings.
Monitor the work of specialists, such as electrical engineers, mechanical engineers, interior designers, or sound specialists to ensure optimal form or function of designs or final structures.
Direct activities of technicians engaged in preparing drawings or specification documents.
Conduct periodic on-site observations of construction work to monitor compliance with plans.
Inspect proposed building sites to determine suitability for construction.
Perform predesign services, such as feasibility or environmental impact studies.
Gather information related to projects' environmental sustainability or operational efficiency.
Develop marketing materials, proposals, or presentations to generate new work opportunities.
Calculate potential energy savings by comparing estimated energy consumption of proposed design to baseline standards.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Artifice DesignWorkshop, Autodesk 3ds Max Design, Autodesk Architectural Studio, Autodesk AutoCAD.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, McNeel Rhinoceros 3D.

skills.name: Desktop publishing software
skills.def: Software to create or edit text and graphics into documents such as books, magazines, brochures, or manuals. Examples: Adobe InDesign, Quark enterprise publishing software.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: BQE Software ArchiOffice, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud EC2, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Web Services AWS software, Database software.

skills.name: Data base management system software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or provide access to a set of related information. Examples: Apache Cassandra, Apache Hadoop, Apache Hive, Apache Pig.
